subject.summary: The Voyager 1 robotic interstellar probe: a 3.66 m high-gain dish on a ten-sided bus, with the three-RTG power boom, the science boom and its two-axis scan platform, the 13 m magnetometer mast, two 10 m whip antennas and the Golden Record bolted to a bus face. Assembled here as a hologram; overall dimensions follow the published figures, the truss detail is traced from photographs.

facts.note: the dish is attached along a 1.78 m support ring
decahedral bus, 1.78 m across flat to flat
graphite-epoxy boom, scan platform at its end
13 m deployable astromast, two low-field sensors
the mast is stowed in a 23 cm cylinder 66 cm long
each RTG 50.8 cm long, three in tandem
two 10 m whip antennas, perpendicular to each other

identity.feature: the 3.66 m shallow parabolic high-gain dish on a short tubular truss over the bus, with the low-gain horn on its tripod above the face
the ten-sided bus, one bay per face, dish face up
three RTGs in tandem on a long down-angled power boom
the science boom carrying the two-axis scan platform with the two vidicon cameras and the baffled IRIS
the 13 m triangular magnetometer astromast, sensors at 10 m and at its tip
two 10 m whip antennas trailing from the bus
the Golden Record bolted flat to a bus face on its mounting plate

next: scan platform: close the two vidicon barrels with a lens plate and shutter, and shape the gimbal as two visible perpendicular rings so the two-axis mount reads in the close view
magnetometer mast: give it a true tapered triangular section and a third longeron that reads at hero scale (it is a 13 m ribbon from most angles)
bus bays: dress six of the ten faces with louvres, the square sunshade and a Canopus star tracker, so no bay is an empty quad up close
the built-in still/side/front framing fits the whole 15.6 m envelope, so the probe is small in those captures; author explicit still views with a tighter fit
assembly: the format caps the build at 20 s; for a 57 s build render the page at 0.35x (tools/slow_render.py does this)
